summary: Clean A2 Dutch: no restricted construction, every sentence ≤ 22 words with ≤ 3 finite verbs, glossary line respected, glosses within limits. The one real quality issue is the compressed simile 'als uit het vuur' in b085; two of the five glosses (drugsgeld, haarnetje) are on transparent compounds and could be dropped.

findings.fragment: trok zijn hand omlaag als uit het vuur
findings.problem: 'als uit het vuur' is not a Dutch idiom; the compressed simile reads as a translation and makes the reader re-parse (as if the hand came out of a fire).
findings.evidence: No Dutch collocation 'als uit het vuur'; the natural form needs 'alsof' (R-CONJ-OTHER), so the comparison must be made explicit instead.
findings.required_fix: Make the comparison explicit with an allowed frame: 'Harry trok zijn hand omlaag, zo snel als uit een vuur, en verstopte de envelop achter zijn rug als \gl{drugsgeld}{drug money}.' Optionally detach the second simile as a fragment: '… achter zijn rug. Als drugsgeld.'

findings.problem: Glossed because the tool rates it hard (nt2lex C1); for the reader it is a transparent compound of two A1 words.
findings.evidence: lexicon: drug = known A1, geld = known A1; bible.md fixes 'drug money' → drugsgeld.
findings.required_fix: Gloss may stay or go; prefer dropping it to keep glosses for real unknowns. Lexicon owner: add 'drugsgeld' as known compound.

findings.problem: Glossed because the tool mis-lemmatises the diminutive to 'haarne'; the word is haar + net + -je, all known.
findings.evidence: lexicon: haar known, net (NOUN) known A1.
findings.required_fix: Gloss optional; dropping it frees one of the two gloss slots in b086. Lexicon owner: add 'haarnetje'.

findings.problem: Unknown lemma, but it carries the scene (embarrassment comedy) and has no plain equivalent with the same meaning for this reader.
findings.evidence: lexicon: gênant absent; 'pijnlijk' (B1) was learned as 'painful', 'stom' shifts the meaning; already glossed.
findings.required_fix: Keep as is. Lexicon owner: consider adding gênant (very frequent spoken word).

findings.problem: Unknown lemma; the plain alternative 'hek' (A2) is an open fence, and the image needs a solid one she must peer over.
findings.evidence: lexicon: schutting absent, hek known A2 'fence'; already glossed.
findings.required_fix: Keep as is; switch to 'het hek van de buren' only if the gloss budget of b086 is needed elsewhere.

findings.fragment: Mevrouw~Figg, af en toe de oppas.
findings.problem: 'af en toe de oppas' is a slightly stiff ellipsis; the possessive reads more naturally.
findings.evidence: Native pattern: 'af en toe zijn oppas' / 'soms zijn oppas'.
findings.required_fix: Prefer 'Mevrouw~Figg, af en toe zijn oppas.'

findings.problem: Gloss on a lemma the lexicon marks known (A2), kept because exceptions.json asks to gloss fluisteren at first occurrence; the two sources disagree.
findings.evidence: lexicon: gefluister known A2 (c4473); exceptions.json keep: fluisteren, gloss 'first'.
findings.required_fix: No change here; profile owner: decide once whether fluisteren/gefluister is known (drop the keep entry) or kept (gloss first).

findings.fragment: ook als ik me dan dom voel
findings.problem: The particle 'dan' inside the als-clause is a small spoken-Dutch filler; without it the clause is cleaner.
findings.evidence: 'ook als ik me dom voel' is the plain form.
findings.required_fix: Optional: 'ook als ik me dom voel'.

findings.problem: Two B1 stretch lemmas in the scene, inside the budget.
findings.evidence: stretch budget 2 vs 8/1000 allowed; both transparent (achter+deur; hersenen recurs for 'brain' per translator note).

flag_decisions.reason: Attributive 'verbaasd' is a plain adjective: lexicon ADJ A1 and named explicitly in restricted.md ('verbaasd … are fine'); look-alike table 'Hij was verbaasd.'

tool_feedback: R-PARTICIPLE on 'verbaasde' (b084) is a false positive: lemma is a lexicon ADJ entry and restricted.md names 'verbaasd' as allowed; skip amod participles whose lemma is a lexicon ADJ, or push confidence under ignore_confidence (0.3).
Vocabulary row 'haarne' is a non-word: spaCy lemma of the diminutive 'haarnetje'; strip -tje/-je before lookup and retry compound decomposition (haar + net) on the stripped form.

'drugsgeld' rated hard C1 (pos VERB) from an nt2lex-only hit; the lexicon hit pre-empts compound decomposition, so a transparent compound of two A1 words is reported as hard and pushed the translator into an unnecessary gloss.

Glosses on known lemmas (gefluister here; 'wilskracht' passes silently as a compound) never appear as a table row, so the reviewer cannot see gloss bloat on known words from the table; add a 'glossed known lemma' row or warning.
